definition: A data object in a protocol specification that distinguishes one protocol object, such as a datagram, interface, endpoint or session, from others of the same type in a given context. It is usually defined as a series of bits and selected dynamically, rather than statically assigned, and has requirements such as uniqueness for a stated period.
plainLanguage: A number a protocol picks at run time to tell one packet, connection or device apart from others of the same kind.
